Three parts

What we will answer

1Where does each item sit on the plot, and why there?→ 2What sits at each elevation, and why?→ 3How does an isometric turn a line into parts, and the layout into a 3-D plant?→

EQL = equipment list; EL = elevation above grade, m; NPSH = net positive suction head; DN = nominal pipe size, mm; SS = stainless steel; LR = long-radius elbow; TBC = to be confirmed; CD = closed drain; NO / NC = normally open / closed; LO / LC = locked (car-sealed) open / closed; PSV = relief valve; AH = analyzer shelter. Line codes: AQ aqueous, SV solvent, RF raffinate, EX extract, VT vent. RDC = rotating-disc contactor; TCE = 1,1,2-trichloroethane; OTS = operator training simulator. Tags use ISA letters: F flow, T temperature, P pressure, L level, S speed, J power, V vibration, A analyzer, H hand; then I indicator, T transmitter, DT differential transmitter, V valve.

Group overview · Engineering (EPC)

Where Layout & isometrics sits in its group

The group asks: Which documents turn the C-101 design into a plant that can be bought, built and started, and how does one change travel through all of them?

  1. Needs before it startsEquipment list and sizes, line list on RDC-PID-002, hazardous zones
  2. Hands onSpacing checks; levels (platform EL 4.2, rack EL 4.5); isometrics and BOMs; the 3-D scene
  3. When in a projectFEED, Detailed engineering

The Engineering (EPC) overview tab, first in the group, shows the whole chain with one worked thread.

Derivation · what the layout gives the pump

Static head at the suction

Grade and EL 1.0 exist for the pumps; how much head does that buy?

$z_L,\ z_s$

$\rho$

kg/m³
$h_s,\ \Delta p_s$

$\Delta p_s=\rho\,g\,h_s/1000$hydrostatics; the layout's share of NPSH

Part 3 · summary

What part 3 settled

  • An isometric turns a line into lengths, elbows, flanges and supports.
  • Seven checks tie the plot, the P&ID lines and the valves.
  • layout.json feeds the 3-D plant: 12 items, 11 runs, 19 instruments, 16 valves.

This deck

Key Takeaways

  • Lay the plot out in the direction of the flow.
  • Check every spacing rule and know its margin.
  • Raise drums for the pumps; put what is read often within reach.
  • Count parts from the isometric: length, elbows, flanges, supports.
  • Keep one layout file behind the plot, the isometrics and the 3-D model.
